reason: The visible function is revised, but the reason given about file detection or parsing errors is speculative.
The chardet sentence is reworded, but the commit does not establish that it was factually inaccurate.
The action version increases, but its status as the latest stable release is unverified.
The tests switch endpoints, but the commit does not establish instability of the old URLs or reliability of the new ones.
The removed code is commented out, but the text does not establish that each line was obsolete.
Deleting the Git requirement is shown, but package-index replacement and the presumed installation motive are speculative.
The newly added sidebar link is for Requests-Toolbelt and the template is not identified as Certifi's documentation.
The explanatory text still makes charset-normalizer conditional on chardet not already being installed.
A bare raise already re-raises the current exception without replacing it with a generic error.
The link label is restyled without evidence that its previous display text contained a typo.
The excerpt shows the README example change but ends before the replacement statistics and FAQ hunk needed to check those claims.
The patch moves or deletes commented code and adds empty branches, but does not establish that the discarded comments were outdated.
The payload is retained initially but is explicitly cleared on several redirect paths.
The excerpt stops within the stylesheet deletion and does not show whether templates were deleted or where the internationalization wrappers went.
The tagline changes, but the source does not explain any change in design philosophy or motive.
The test changes the form input, but it does not validate the behavior of the test method itself.
The note describes a ConnectionError mistakenly reported as ConnectTimeout, not a change to the handling of actual timeouts.
The command stops requesting colored output, but the source does not establish any broader simplification of test execution.
Removing the handler lets certain conversion errors propagate, but not all malformed percent sequences reach conversion.
The import becomes relative, but the commit does not establish package behavior across the installation and Python-path scenarios claimed.
The clone URL changes to HTTPS, but the source does not identify a deprecation or blocked ports.
The helper now always sends an empty string and ignores a caller-supplied data value.
The excerpt cuts off before the end of the expanded file, so there is no evidence of its final newline.
The title and file list support the vendored library switch but do not demonstrate continuity of encoding detection.
The helper extraction and new tests are shown, but the stated improvement in parsing robustness is unverified.
The pytest lower bound is shown, but compatibility of every allowed version is not established.
The caller passes a URL, but the new credential lookup uses self.url rather than that argument.
The manifest lists these files for future source distributions without showing that they were omitted from earlier builds.
The copyright year advances to 2017, but the source does not establish that this was the current year.
The relative import is shown, but the commit does not establish that users previously encountered installation-specific import failures.
The external image is removed, but the commit does not say that the image was outdated.
The listed encodings change, but the header gives them no explicit preference weights.
The added registry section contains incomplete prose and an unfinished example rather than a feature description.
The guide explains how to add cookies manually if desired, without imposing manual management for session cookies generally.
